public_rationale: The Register reported that on 5 January 2025 Sam Altman posted that OpenAI was "currently losing money on OpenAI Pro subscriptions" (e1). The same report says the $200-a-month Pro tier, announced about a month earlier, gives unlimited access to the o1 pro model (e2). This points the same way as Marcus's claim. But it covers one subscription tier, not o1 as a product. The contract asks for o1's profit or loss across all the ways it was sold in December 2024 to January 2025. Neither item gives o1's revenue or serving costs at that level. Nothing in the evidence shows o1 was profitable either. The evidence does not support or contradict the claim as the contract reads it.
limitations: The evidence covers only the ChatGPT Pro tier. It does not cover o1 sold through other channels, such as ChatGPT Plus or the API.
Altman's post gives no figures for Pro revenue or costs.
If "o1" were read as only the o1 pro tier, Altman's statement would bear more directly on the claim. The outcome depends on that reading.
OpenAI's company-wide losses are a different measure and do not isolate o1.

criteria.contradiction_condition: An OpenAI disclosure or credible report that o1 was profitable or covered its costs in that period.
